Jim stood in the back of the studio, sweating profusely as he attempted to mimic the instructor’s graceful "Tree Pose." He was less of a tree and more of a wind-blown shrub. The class, a group of serene yogis, tried to ignore the symphony of grunts and accidental toots emanating from Jim, but it was impossible.

Just as the instructor commanded, "Now, extend your neck to release tension," Jim, confused and trying to look like the others, craned his head upward with exaggerated effort. He wasn't a giraffe, but in his desperation to reach the heavens, he looked remarkably like one. The class couldn't help but giggle as Jim wobbled, his long neck stretching comically high, turning the zen session into a circus act. The humor wasn't just in the noise, but in the visual of a man contorting himself into a shape that defied both yoga and anatomy, all while maintaining a look of intense, misguided concentration.
